## What This Page Shows

This page describes the automation layer around the Omega project as a set of research directions, not as a list of names, examples, or historical log entries.

The priority order is deliberate. The main line is the **formalization pipeline**: extending the verified kernel, preserving conservative-extension discipline, and turning mathematical claims into Lean-checkable artifacts. The paper and outreach systems are useful, but they are supporting channels. They package, stress-test, explain, and distribute what the formal core can actually support.

The distinctive mechanism is not a one-shot prompt. It is supervised self-iteration: agents read the current input, produce an output, pass it through deterministic and mathematical gates, then use the resulting failures, diffs, logs, and review signals as the next input. The supervisor keeps that input-output loop coherent: it claims work, watches health, detects stalling, routes failures to the right agent or gate, and prevents unreviewed material from escaping.

The boundary is also deliberate: the system may draft, check, route, and organize, but external communication and publication decisions remain human-approved.

The lower layers are not separate goals. They are ways of making the extension core useful: papers expose formal content to mathematical readers, deepening turns weak drafts into stronger claims or honest obstructions, and outreach looks for places where existing structural evidence can help an external problem.

## Shared Control Surface

All directions use the same operating pattern: a supervisor turns agent work into a self-iterating research loop. It is not only a process watchdog. It maintains task claims, chooses the next action from current evidence, compares input/output against gates, recognizes no-progress cycles, recovers stale state, and routes failures back into proof repair, paper repair, deeper reasoning, or human review. Deterministic gates handle routine state; LLM agents are used only where judgment or synthesis is useful; every outward-facing artifact lands in a reviewable draft state before it can leave the machine.

```text
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ supervisor                                     │
        │ - claim work and monitor worker health          │
        │ - read input, output, diffs, logs, and gates    │
        │ - detect stalling and repeated failure modes    │
        │ - choose retry / rescope / deepen / review      │
        └───────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        v
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ deterministic gates                             │
        │ - build / proof / import checks                 │
        │ - freshness / dedup / preflight                 │
        │ - board state / task claims / retry budgets     │
        │ - file presence / size / contract checks        │
        └───────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        v
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ judgment agents                                 │
        │ - code and proof repair                         │
        │ - paper synthesis and critique                  │
        │ - attached-context mathematical reasoning       │
        │ - scoped drafting for human review              │
        └───────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │ output
                        v
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ reviewable artifact                             │
        │ - Lean patch / local note / paper section       │
        │ - evidence packet / draft reply / review memo   │
        │ - no automatic email, post, or submission       │
        └───────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │ gate result / diff / review signal
                        └─────────────── back to supervisor
```

In other words, the pipeline is a closed research control loop. A worker does not merely produce text; it produces a state transition. The supervisor decides whether that transition is progress, noise, a reusable obstruction, or a reason to change strategy.

## 1. Formalization and Extension Core

This is the primary pipeline. Its job is to grow the verified kernel without weakening earlier layers. Every new interface should either be formally checked, reduced to a precise local obligation, or rejected as too speculative for the kernel.

```text
 CLAIM / EXTENSION SOURCES
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ paper theorem environments                              │
 │ existing Lean declarations                              │
 │ extension-core interfaces                               │
 │ conservative-extension obligations                      │
 │ failed proof attempts and missing lemmas                │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 TARGET SELECTION
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ formalization planner                                   │
 │ - locate claims without Lean support                    │
 │ - prioritize kernel-relevant extension obligations      │
 │ - avoid duplicate or already-claimed targets            │
 │ - keep speculative claims outside the verified core     │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 PROOF WORK LOOP
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Lean patch generation and repair                        │
 │ - isolated worktrees for parallel proof attempts        │
 │ - import and namespace hygiene                          │
 │ - theorem statement stabilization                       │
 │ - proof search, simplification, and refactoring         │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 KERNEL GATES
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ verification gates                                      │
 │ - Lean build succeeds                                   │
 │ - no accidental axiom / sorry / placeholder leakage     │
 │ - declarations match paper labels where applicable      │
 │ - extension does not silently redefine lower layers     │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 VERIFIED CORE UPDATE
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ accepted Lean artifact                                  │
 │ - new theorem, definition, interface, or regression     │
 │ - paper-facing label or source map when useful          │
 │ - reusable evidence for later papers and outreach       │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The core question is always: does this extend the verified structure without breaking the meaning of what came before? If the answer is unclear, the pipeline should produce a smaller lemma, a counterexample, or a clear obstruction rather than a stronger-looking but unsupported claim.

## 2. Paper Automation Pipeline

The paper automation pipeline packages verified and near-verified material into manuscripts. It is not the source of mathematical authority. Its value is operational: keeping many paper projects buildable, reviewable, and aligned with the formal core.

```text
 PAPER SOURCES
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ TeX manuscript trees                                    │
 │ theorem labels and source maps                          │
 │ Lean-backed result inventories                          │
 │ bibliography and journal-profile context                │
 │ pipeline state from previous review rounds              │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 ASSEMBLY
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ publication pipeline                                    │
 │ - structure and section planning                        │
 │ - claim inventory and paper-local scope contract        │
 │ - bibliography normalization                            │
 │ - journal-style rewrite when appropriate                │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 BUILD + CONSISTENCY GATES
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ manuscript checks                                       │
 │ - LaTeX builds                                          │
 │ - labels and references resolve                         │
 │ - theorem strength matches available evidence           │
 │ - submission checklist is explicit                      │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 REVIEWABLE PAPER ARTIFACT
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ local manuscript state                                  │
 │ - draft / revised draft / submission-ready packet       │
 │ - never treated as public without human approval        │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

This pipeline should follow the formal core. When the manuscript says more than the kernel or audited derivation supports, the paper pipeline must weaken the claim, mark it as conjectural, or route it to paper deepening.

## 3. Paper Deepening Pipeline

The deepening pipeline is the bridge between draft text and real mathematical substance. It audits weak claims, asks for missing lemmas, tests whether a proof route can be made precise, and writes back only what survives review.

```text
 WEAK OR UNFINISHED MATERIAL
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ proof gaps                                              │
 │ referee-style objections                                │
 │ unsupported theorem-strength phrasing                   │
 │ unclear relation between TeX and Lean                   │
 │ stale or over-broad manuscript sections                 │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 DEEPENING PASS
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ mathematical repair                                     │
 │ - isolate the exact missing claim                       │
 │ - search for a smaller theorem                          │
 │ - produce obstruction or counterexample when needed     │
 │ - identify the Lean target if formalization is feasible │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 WRITEBACK DISCIPLINE
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ accepted paper-local update                             │
 │ - theorem strengthened only when evidence improves      │
 │ - unsupported content demoted to remark/open problem    │
 │ - formalization handoff created for kernel-relevant     │
 │   claims                                                │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Deepening is not public presentation. It is internal pressure: if a manuscript claim is weak, either make it true, make it smaller, or mark the obstruction honestly.

## 4. Outreach and Open-Problem Pipeline

Outreach is a supporting channel, not the center of the system. Its job is to route existing evidence toward useful external contexts: open problems, collaborator threads, issue discussions, and short explanatory notes. It should never outrun the verified core.

```text
 SIGNALS
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ public open problems                                    │
 │ existing collaboration threads                          │
 │ issue / PR contexts already under discussion            │
 │ papers or claims that need a scoped response            │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 TRIAGE
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ outreach gates                                          │
 │ - freshness and relevance                               │
 │ - can the formal/paper evidence actually help?          │
 │ - is there a concrete artifact and audience?            │
 │ - if not, drop or defer                                 │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 EVIDENCE PACKET
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ local research packet                                   │
 │ - problem statement                                     │
 │ - verified or audited evidence                          │
 │ - known gaps and non-claims                             │
 │ - exact mathematical question for deeper reasoning      │
 └──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            v
 HUMAN-REVIEWED OUTPUT
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ possible artifact                                       │
 │ - author email draft                                    │
 │ - issue comment draft                                   │
 │ - short note                                            │
 │ - formalization handoff                                 │
 │ - paper-local writeback                                 │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The outreach loop should stop when the evidence is only promotional. It should continue only when it can produce a bounded mathematical contribution, a useful obstruction, or a clearly scoped question for another researcher.

## Shared Safety Rules

The pipelines are allowed to be persistent, but not autonomous in the publication sense.

```text
 allowed automatically
 ├─ refresh targeted context
 ├─ recover stale task claims
 ├─ run deterministic gates
 ├─ draft local artifacts
 ├─ update local review queues
 └─ propose maintenance actions

 requires human approval
 ├─ send email
 ├─ post to GitHub / X / forum
 ├─ submit a paper
 ├─ publish a claim externally
 └─ push public-facing intermediate material
```

Intermediate artifacts are local by default. Deterministic gates are preferred whenever code can make the decision reliably. LLM calls are reserved for synthesis, judgment, and language tasks that cannot be stabilized cheaply in code.

## Artifact Types

The system produces artifacts that can be reviewed, edited, and either approved or rejected.

| Artifact | Primary direction | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| Lean patch | formalization core | formalize or repair a claim |
| extension interface note | formalization core | define the next conservative layer boundary |
| paper section draft | paper automation | move verified or scoped material into a manuscript |
| referee memo | paper deepening | identify proof gaps, overclaims, and missing lemmas |
| obstruction note | paper deepening / outreach | record why a route currently fails |
| evidence packet | outreach / deep reasoning | bundle the problem, checked evidence, gaps, and exact question |
| author email or issue draft | outreach | ask for or contribute a bounded next step |
| media packet | outreach | present an already supported result after review |

## Where This Is Going

The long-term goal is not to automate mathematical publication end to end. The goal is to make AI-assisted research legible, auditable, and useful enough that humans can spend more time judging mathematical substance and less time moving context between tools.

For this project, the main output is the extension core: a growing verified structure whose lower layers remain stable while new layers add expressive power. The paper pipelines exist to make that structure readable and publishable. The outreach pipeline exists to find places where the structure can be tested, explained, or applied. Public communication is downstream of mathematical support, not a substitute for it.
